struck: A home that is not the owner's legal residence, which includes every rental, is taxed in South Carolina on 6 percent of its value.
use: A home that is not its owner's legal residence, such as a house rented out year-round or a second home, is taxed on 6 percent of its value.

pattern: rented (for )?more than (72|seventy-two) days[^.]{0,80}(cannot|can't|can never|may not) keep
struck: A home rented more than 72 days in a year cannot keep the 4 percent rate.
use: A legal residence rented out more than 72 days in a calendar year loses the 4 percent rate, unless its owner is on active military duty under orders.

struck: A rental pays all of it: 109.1 mills in Horry County for 2026, the largest line on the bill.
use: A rental pays all of it: 109.1 mills in Horry County for 2026, the largest line on the bill everywhere but Loris.
(cut Aynor from the calculator until the town's fire millage is confirmed: county fire millage also applies in a town that contracts with the county for fire protection)

struck: So the buyer's first October bill still uses the seller's value; the next one uses the new value.
use: If you buy between January and September, your first October bill still uses the seller's value, and the next one uses the new value. Buy in October or later, and your first bill already uses the new value.

pattern: (4 percent|four percent|legal residence|seller lived|owner-occupied|lived in)(?:[^.]|\.\d){0,120}25 percent (exemption|off)|25 percent (exemption|off)(?:[^.]|\.\d){0,120}(4 percent|four percent|legal residence|seller lived|owner-occupied)
struck: Buying a home the seller lived in, the tax is about 3.6 times the seller's bill with the 25 percent exemption claimed.
use: The 25 percent exemption applies only when the home was taxed at 6 percent before the sale and stays at 6 percent after it.

struck: Half of this year's resales were the seller's own home on the county record.
use: Half of this year's resales (4,223 of 8,310) carried the 4 percent legal-residence rate on the county's record for 2026.

struck: Buying a home the seller lived in, the tax is about 3.6 to 3.9 times the seller's bill. The middle half runs about 3.3 to 4.8 times.
use: When the 2026 record was 4 percent, an investor's next bill at the sale price is about 3.9 times the seller's. The middle half runs about 3.4 to 4.8 times.

struck: HUD sets the fair market rent for each ZIP code at the 40th percentile of gross rent for a standard unit.
use: HUD sets its fair market rent at the 40th percentile of rent plus utilities for a standard unit across the metro area, then adjusts it for each ZIP code.

struck: Of 1,785 condos with 2 or more bedrooms for sale in Horry County, 214 ask 100 times HUD's 2-bedroom rent or less.
use: Of 1,785 condos with 2 or more bedrooms for sale in the 10 ZIP codes we tested, 214 ask 100 times HUD's 2-bedroom rent or less.

struck: About half of condos for sale charge $600 a month or more.
use: More than half of condos for sale (1,552 of 2,828) list dues over $600 a month. The middle condo's dues are between $600 and $700.

struck: A 3-bedroom house in Longs, unincorporated Horry County: tax about $3,860.
use: A 3-bedroom house in Longs, outside city limits: tax about $3,860.

struck: Management 10 percent and repairs 10 percent are the owner's figures.
use: We allow 10 percent of the rent for management and 10 percent for repairs and empty months.

struck: We get an insurance quote for the address before you offer.
use: We can get you an insurance quote for the house before you make an offer.
